editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.110, Regular rings and global dimension. It proves equivalences between regularity of Noetherian local rings and finiteness of projective/global dimension using previously defined regularity, module projective dimension and ring global dimension. The section does not add a distinct standalone definition represented by its joint theorem heading.

Read Stacks 10.121, Definitions 10.121.2, 10.121.3 and 10.121.5. It defines order of vanishing for a one-dimensional local Noetherian domain and also lattices and their distance in finite-dimensional fraction-field vector spaces.

definitions.text: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain R with fraction field K, the order of vanishing of a nonzero a∈R is length_R(R/(a)); it extends to K× by ord_R(a/b)=length_R(R/(a))−length_R(R/(b)).
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: order of vanishing along a one-dimensional local domain

definitions.text: For a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain R with fraction field K and finite-dimensional K-vector space V, an R-lattice in V is a finite R-submodule M⊆V whose K-span equals V.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: R-lattice in a finite-dimensional vector space

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.107, Lemma 10.107.1. An epimorphism of commutative rings is categorical, not necessarily a surjective map of underlying sets; equivalently its multiplication map S⊗_R S→S is an isomorphism.

definitions.text: A ring homomorphism f:R→S is an epimorphism in the category of commutative rings if every pair of ring maps g,h:S→T satisfying g∘f=h∘f are equal; equivalently the multiplication map S⊗_R S→S is an isomorphism.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: categorical epimorphism of rings

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.117, 'Dimension of graded algebras over a field'. Lemmas relate Hilbert polynomials and Krull dimension for standard graded finite-type algebras, using previously defined dimension and Hilbert polynomial notions, but no separate definition corresponding to the section heading is introduced.

Read Stacks 10.34, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz. The section states and proves the theorem on maximal ideals of finite-type algebras over fields and its radical-ideal consequence. This is a theorem, not a new definition of a mathematical object called the 'Nullstellensatz'.

Read Stacks 10.91 on examples and counterexamples of Mittag-Leffler modules. It illustrates the definition developed in its preceding module section and proves examples and failures, rather than introducing an independent object named by the section heading.

Read Stacks Categories 4.19, Definition 4.19.1. Filtered or directed categories require nonemptiness, existence of a common receiving object for any pair of objects, and eventual equalization of parallel arrows.

definitions.text: A category I is filtered if it is nonempty, any two objects admit arrows into a common object, and every pair of parallel arrows u,v:i⇉j can be equalized after an arrow j→k.
A filtered colimit is a colimit of a diagram F:I→C indexed by a filtered category I; in Sets it identifies elements that become equal at some later common stage.
definitions.context_hint: Category theory: filtered colimit of a diagram

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Categories 4.44, Definition 4.44.1. It defines a category of dotted arrows associated to a partially specified 2-commutative square, whose objects are completions by a diagonal 1-morphism and compatible 2-isomorphisms.

definitions.text: Given a fixed 2-commutative solid square in a (2,1)-category, its category of dotted arrows has objects the possible diagonal 1-morphisms completing the square together with specified compatible invertible 2-morphisms, and morphisms the 2-isomorphisms respecting these data.
definitions.context_hint: Higher category theory: category of dotted-arrow fillers

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.164 on descending properties for flat ring maps and their modules. The lemmas prove that Noetherianity, reducedness, normality and other previously defined properties descend under faithfully flat maps in appropriate settings. No new standalone object named 'descending properties' is defined.

Read Stacks Categories 4.20, introductory explanation of duality between filtered colimits and cofiltered limits. A cofiltered indexing category has common predecessors and can equalize arrows after precomposition.

definitions.text: A category I is cofiltered if its opposite category I^op is filtered; equivalently I is nonempty, any two objects receive arrows from a common object, and any parallel arrows become equal after precomposition from another object.

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.48, Definition 10.48.3 and Lemma 10.48.2. Geometrical connectedness of a k-algebra concerns connectivity of its spectrum after all extensions of the ground field.

definitions.text: A k-algebra A is geometrically connected if for every field extension K/k the topological space Spec(A⊗_k K) is connected.

editorial_reason: Read Stacks Topology 5.14 on limits of topological spaces. Its explicit construction realizes a limit as the compatible-tuples subspace of the product of the component spaces, which is a precise mathematical description.

definitions.text: The limit of a diagram of topological spaces (X_i,f_{ij}) is the subset of the product ∏_i X_i consisting of all families (x_i) compatible with the diagram maps, equipped with its subspace topology from the product.
definitions.source_section: Section 5.14 construction of limits in Top

editorial_reason: Read Stacks 10.123 on Zariski's Main Theorem. It establishes factorization and finiteness properties of quasi-finite algebra maps using definitions established in preceding sections; the named theorem itself is not a separate definable object.

Read Stacks 10.80 on faithfully flat descent for projectivity. Its main lemma proves descent of finite projectivity under faithfully flat base change, relying on previously defined faithfully flat maps and projective modules. There is no distinct definition under this theorem heading.

Read Stacks 10.97 on completion of Noetherian rings. It describes the I-adic completion as inverse limit of quotients and the special properties for a Noetherian ring, giving an equivalent characterization useful to distinguish a completion ring from a completed module.

definitions.text: For a Noetherian commutative ring R and ideal I, the I-adic completion R^ is the inverse-limit ring lim_n R/I^n, with structure homomorphism R→R^ induced by the quotient maps.
definitions.context_hint: Commutative algebra: I-adic completion of a Noetherian ring
